meta.label: Money transfer and remittance
tradeoffLabels: least lost to fees and the exchange-rate margin
reaches the most people, including cash pickup
meta.attribution: Compares ways to send money to another country from the US, the UK and the EU: money transfer companies, a bank wire and a bank's own remittance product, a PayPal payment, and the route of sending a dollar stablecoin. Fees: the World Bank's Remittance Prices Worldwide complete dataset (Q3 2025 survey, collected in August 2025; catalogue updated September 2026) prices each service for sending the equivalent of $200 and $500 in each corridor, recording the transfer fee, the exchange-rate margin over the interbank rate, and the total cost. For each provider this comparison takes every corridor the World Bank priced from the US, the UK or an EU country, finds the provider's cheapest service in each, and uses the median of those total costs for $200; the score is 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost (floor 5). US to Mexico and UK to India are quoted where the provider was priced there. PayPal is not in the survey, so its cost is derived from PayPal's own fee table on the same scale. Transparency: the median exchange-rate margin across all the provider's priced services in the same data, the part of the price hidden inside the rate rather than shown as a fee; the score is 100 minus 15 points per percentage point. Where the conversion happens after the money leaves (a US-dollar bank wire) or is set by an exchange (stablecoins), that is said and scored by judgement or left empty. Complaint record: regulator enforcement and ombudsman outcomes, starting at 80 for a clean record. Deductions are made for consumer-protection orders since 2020 in the CFPB's enforcement actions list and for the FTC's Western Union case, sized by scale and seriousness, and for a Financial Ombudsman Service uphold rate above the 26% banking and credit average in its July 2025 to March 2026 business data (a below-average rate adds 5). CFPB complaint counts for 2024 and 2025 are reported in notes as raw numbers, not scored, because they are not adjusted for customer numbers. The stablecoin route is scored for recourse, using the FTC's guidance that crypto payments typically cannot be reversed. Reach: what each provider's own site or App Store listing says about countries served, cash pickup, mobile money and agent locations, scored by judgement (agent cash networks in 200 countries highest, account-holders-only routes lowest). Not scored: speed, which varies by corridor and payout method; promotional first-transfer offers; and amounts other than $200. Wise is checked against the CFPB's 2025 order, MoneyGram against the 2022 CFPB and New York lawsuit, Sendwave against the 2023 CFPB order, and Intermex's pending sale to Western Union against its October 2026 SEC filing. Revolut's own fee pages and TransferGo's regulatory record could not be checked, so Revolut's figures rest on a two-corridor sample and TransferGo has no complaint score. Sources: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide (dataset and Q3 2025 report), the CFPB enforcement actions list and complaint database, the FTC, the Financial Ombudsman Service, the SEC's EDGAR, and each provider's own pricing, terms or App Store pages. Prices and rates change daily: check the live quote before sending. Not financial advice. Reviewed 2026-10.

reads.text: Compare money transfer and remittance by fees, everyday access, disclosure, and complaint record.

criteria.label: Low total cost to send $200 (fee plus exchange-rate margin)
Little of the price hidden in the exchange rate
Regulator and ombudsman record, and recourse when things go wrong
Reach: countries served, cash pickup, ways to send

products.name: Wise
products.description: An online money transfer service that converts at the mid-market rate and charges a separate, upfront fee. Among the cheapest of the large providers in the World Bank's data, with almost nothing hidden in the rate, but it delivers to accounts rather than cash pickup points.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 74 corridors where Wise was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 2.21%. Representative corridors: US to Mexico 1.26%; UK to India 1.09%. Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin Wise applied above the interbank rate, across its 197 priced services in 74 corridors, was 0.01%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). Wise's own US pricing page states that it uses only the live mid-market rate plus a small upfront fee. Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: On January 30, 2025 the CFPB issued an order against Wise US Inc. over deceptive marketing of ATM fees and failures in remittance disclosures and error resolution; the May 15, 2025 amended order requires about $450,000 in consumer redress and a $44,955 civil money penalty. In the UK, the Financial Ombudsman Service upheld 19% of the Wise Payments Limited complaints it resolved from July 2025 to March 2026, against a 26% average for banking and credit. Scored 80, minus 20 for a CFPB order since 2020, plus 5 for a below-average ombudsman uphold rate.

accessibility.note: Wise's US site says transfers deliver to 140+ countries and that the account works in 40+ currencies. Sending and receiving is online or in the app into bank accounts and similar; the World Bank sampled no cash or agent service from Wise.

links.label: Financial Ombudsman Service complaints data H2 2025
World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: Remitly
products.description: An app-based remittance service built for people sending money home, with delivery to bank accounts, mobile wallets and cash pickup. Mid-table on cost in the World Bank data, with more of its price inside the exchange rate than Wise.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 127 corridors where Remitly was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 3.01%. Representative corridors: US to Mexico 5.38%; UK to India 2.11%. Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin Remitly applied above the interbank rate, across its 603 priced services in 127 corridors, was 1.28%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: The Financial Ombudsman Service upheld 29% of the complaints about REMITLY U.K., LTD that it resolved from July 2025 to March 2026, slightly above the 26% average for banking and credit. No CFPB remittance enforcement action against Remitly was found in the CFPB's list (checked October 2026); the CFPB complaint database holds 336 money transfer complaints filed under Remitly, Inc. for 2024 and 2025. Scored 80, minus 5 for an above-average ombudsman uphold rate.

accessibility.note: Remitly's US site says it serves 175+ countries and that recipients can be paid to a bank account, mobile wallet or cash pickup location. Sending is through the app or website only.

links.label: Financial Ombudsman Service complaints data H2 2025
World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: Western Union
products.description: A cash and digital transfer network with 600,000 agent locations, sending online, by app or in person to 200+ countries. Reach is unmatched; cost sits above the digital specialists in the World Bank data, and its record includes a $586 million US fraud settlement.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 168 corridors where Western Union was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 3.89%. Representative corridors: US to Mexico 3.90%; UK to India 0.98%. Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin Western Union applied above the interbank rate, across its 587 priced services in 168 corridors, was 1.65%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). Western Union's own US site adds that it also makes money from currency exchange, and its terms say consumer rates are set by adding a margin to interbank rates. Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: The FTC's case page records Western Union's January 2017 settlement with the FTC and Justice Department, in which it admitted anti-money-laundering violations, settled consumer fraud charges and forfeited $586 million; refunds of $153 million (March 2020) and $147 million (September 2020) went to fraud victims. The case page was last updated in September 2020 and was re-read in October 2026. Scored 80, minus 45 for a large consumer-harm settlement with an order still governing how it handles fraud-induced transfers.

accessibility.note: Western Union's US site states it sends to 200+ countries and territories, through 600,000 agent locations worldwide, online, in the app or in person, with cash pickup, bank account and mobile wallet delivery.

links.label: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: MoneyGram
products.description: A global cash and digital money transfer network reaching 200+ countries through partners from banks to corner shops. Cheaper than Western Union in the World Bank data, but with a long US enforcement history.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 165 corridors where MoneyGram was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 2.86%. Representative corridors: US to Mexico 1.71%; UK to India 1.91%. Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin MoneyGram applied above the interbank rate, across its 519 priced services in 165 corridors, was 0.93%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: The CFPB's page records the April 2022 lawsuit it filed jointly with the New York Attorney General against MoneyGram under the Remittance Transfer Rule, announced as 'CFPB and NY Attorney General Sue Repeat Offender MoneyGram For Leaving Families High and Dry'. The CFPB withdrew as a plaintiff in April 2025; the page does not record the outcome of the state's claims. Scored 80, minus 50 for a repeat-offender lawsuit by two regulators since 2020.

accessibility.note: MoneyGram's US site says it has partners across more than 200 countries and territories and that you can send in the app, online or in person, with cash pickup, bank account, debit card or digital wallet delivery depending on the country.

links.label: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: Xoom
products.description: PayPal's remittance service, sending to bank accounts, cards, mobile wallets and cash pickup. Very cheap on US to Mexico in the World Bank data but expensive on many other routes, because a large share of its price sits in the exchange rate.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 47 corridors where Xoom was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 4.59%. Representative corridors: US to Mexico -0.24%; UK to India 3.07%. Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin Xoom applied above the interbank rate, across its 144 priced services in 47 corridors, was 2.96%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). Xoom's own site states that in addition to transaction fees it makes money when it changes your send currency into a different currency. Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: No consumer-protection enforcement action against Xoom appears in the CFPB's list of remittance enforcement actions (checked October 2026). The CFPB complaint database holds 27 complaints filed under XOOM CORPORATION about money transfer services received January 2024 to December 2025, a raw count not adjusted for customer numbers. Xoom is a PayPal service; PayPal's own UK record is scored on its own entry. Scored 80, the method's starting point for a clean record.

accessibility.note: Xoom's site offers transfers to bank accounts and debit cards, to mobile wallets, UPI and PIX, and cash for pickup and delivery. Sending is online or in the app, funded from a bank account, card or PayPal balance.

links.label: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: Revolut
products.description: A finance app whose transfers go to bank accounts in 160+ countries. Cheap in the two corridors the World Bank priced, but the sample is very small and both people need to work within Revolut's app and plan limits.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 2 corridors where Revolut was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 1.55%. The World Bank priced Revolut in only two corridors (Germany to Kosovo 0.30%, UK to Albania 2.81%), so this figure is thin. Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin Revolut applied above the interbank rate, across its 3 priced services in 2 corridors, was 0.31%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). Only three Revolut services were priced. Revolut's own fee pages could not be opened for this check, so plan allowances and any weekend markup are not reflected. Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: The Financial Ombudsman Service upheld 26% of the Revolut Ltd complaints it resolved from July 2025 to March 2026, level with the 26% average for banking and credit. No CFPB remittance enforcement action against Revolut was found (checked October 2026). Scored 80, the method's starting point.

accessibility.note: Revolut's UK App Store listing says the app sends to traditional bank accounts in 160+ countries, and that product availability varies by jurisdiction. The sender needs a Revolut account; the World Bank sampled no cash pickup service.

links.label: Financial Ombudsman Service complaints data H2 2025
World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: Ria Money Transfer
products.description: A large cash and digital remittance network sending to 190+ countries with half a million cash pickup points. Costs sit in the middle of the pack in the World Bank data.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 146 corridors where Ria was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 3.73%. Representative corridors: US to Mexico 2.24%; UK to India 2.51%. Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin Ria applied above the interbank rate, across its 401 priced services in 146 corridors, was 1.30%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: No consumer-protection enforcement action against Ria appears in the CFPB's list of remittance enforcement actions (checked October 2026). The CFPB complaint database holds 112 complaints filed under Ria Envia, LLC about money transfer services received January 2024 to December 2025, a raw count not adjusted for customer numbers. Scored 80, the method's starting point for a clean record.

accessibility.note: Ria's US App Store listing says it sends to over 190 countries and territories, to over 500,000 cash pickup locations, with cash pickup, bank deposit, mobile wallet or home delivery, paid by debit card, bank account or credit card. Ria also operates through agent stores.

links.label: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: WorldRemit
products.description: A digital remittance service, part of the Zepz group alongside Sendwave, paying out to bank accounts, mobile money and cash pickup in 130+ countries. Moderately priced in the World Bank data.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 70 corridors where WorldRemit was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 2.74%. Representative corridors: UK to India 2.29%. Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin WorldRemit applied above the interbank rate, across its 221 priced services in 70 corridors, was 1.45%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: No consumer-protection enforcement action against WorldRemit appears in the CFPB's list of remittance enforcement actions (checked October 2026). The CFPB complaint database holds 68 complaints filed under WorldRemit Corp. about money transfer services received January 2024 to December 2025, a raw count not adjusted for customer numbers. Its sister brand Sendwave, licensed in the US through WorldRemit Corp., was the subject of a 2023 CFPB order scored on its own entry. Scored 80, the method's starting point for a clean record.

accessibility.note: WorldRemit's About page says it covers 130+ countries and 70+ currencies, with bank transfer, mobile money and cash pickup options, sent online or in its app.

links.label: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: Sendwave
products.description: An app for sending money mainly to Africa and Asia with no transfer fee on many routes, operated by Zepz. Cheap in the World Bank sample; the CFPB found in 2023 that it had misrepresented the speed and cost of its transfers.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 7 corridors where Sendwave was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 1.08%. Sendwave was priced from Germany and the UK only, mostly to African corridors (UK to Nigeria -0.12%, UK to Kenya 0.38%). Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin Sendwave applied above the interbank rate, across its 14 priced services in 7 corridors, was 1.18%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). Sendwave usually charges no fee, so its margin is most of what a sender pays. Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: On October 17, 2023 the CFPB issued an order against Chime, Inc. doing business as Sendwave, finding it misrepresented the speed and cost of its remittance transfers, wrongly required customers to waive their rights, failed to give required disclosures including the exchange rate, and failed to investigate errors properly. The order required about $1.5 million in redress and a $1.5 million civil money penalty. Scored 80, minus 25 for a CFPB order since 2020 that went to the core of its remittance disclosures.

accessibility.note: Sendwave's countries hub lists 55 destination countries, mainly in Africa and Asia plus parts of Latin America, sent from the US, Canada, the UK and several EU countries. Sending is app-only, linked to a debit card.

links.label: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: PayPal international personal payment
products.description: Sending money abroad from one PayPal account to another. Convenient if both people already use PayPal, but the international fee plus a 4% currency conversion spread make it one of the dearer ways to send a typical amount.

fees.note: PayPal's US consumer fees page lists an additional 5% international fee on personal transactions (minimum $0.99, maximum $4.99) and a 4.00% currency conversion spread when the recipient receives a different currency. On $200 from a PayPal balance that is $4.99 (2.5%) plus 4%, about 6.5% in total. PayPal is not in the World Bank survey; this figure is derived from PayPal's own fee table and scored on the same scale (100 minus 10 per percentage point).

transparency.note: PayPal's fee table states its 4.00% currency conversion spread outright, which is more candid than an unstated markup, but the spread is still carried inside the exchange rate rather than shown as a fee. Scored on the same scale as the World Bank margins (100 minus 15 per percentage point).

complaints.note: The Financial Ombudsman Service upheld 38% of the PayPal UK Ltd complaints it resolved from July 2025 to March 2026, well above the 26% average for banking and credit; PayPal UK drew 1,915 new ombudsman cases in the period. Scored 80, minus 20 for a well above-average uphold rate.

accessibility.note: PayPal's fee page defines an international transaction as one where sender and receiver are registered with PayPal as residents of different markets, so both people need PayPal accounts; there is no cash pickup.

links.label: Financial Ombudsman Service complaints data H2 2025

products.name: Bank of America international wire
products.description: The big-bank route: a wire from your checking account. Bank of America charges $45 to wire US dollars abroad, which on a $200 transfer is the most expensive option here, and the conversion cost at the other end is not known when you send.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 12 corridors where Bank of America, Chase or Citibank was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 17.50%. Representative corridors: US to Mexico 17.50%. The three big US banks were pooled because each was priced in only a few corridors; their flat wire fees of $35 to $50 are 17.5% to 25% of $200. Bank of America's own page lists $45 for an international wire in US dollars. Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: Bank of America's wire page says that when you send US dollars to an account in another currency, the payment is converted by an intermediary or receiving bank: 'We are not responsible for the exchange rate applied by any intermediary bank or the receiving bank.' For foreign-currency wires it says 'No wire transfer fee, but exchange rate markups apply.' The World Bank's records for these wires show a 0% margin only because the conversion happens after the money leaves the bank, and note that an account is required for detailed price information. Scored 25 by judgement: the sender cannot see the full cost before paying.

complaints.note: On July 11, 2023 the CFPB ordered Bank of America to refund about $80.4 million in repeat non-sufficient-funds fees and pay a $60 million civil penalty, alongside a separate $60 million OCC fine; the CFPB's press release for the action also covered withheld credit card rewards and accounts opened without consent. Not a wire-transfer case, but the bank's consumer record. Scored 80, minus 40 for large consumer-protection orders since 2020.

accessibility.note: Bank of America's wire page describes international wires sent from your own account online or in a financial center, typically credited in 1 to 2 business days. Only account holders can send, and the recipient needs a bank account.

links.label: CFPB: Bank of America fees order
World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: Wells Fargo ExpressSend
products.description: A US bank's own remittance product for its customers, sending to Latin America, the Caribbean and Asia. Far cheaper than a bank wire in the World Bank data, but only for Wells Fargo account holders and only to a limited set of regions.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 9 corridors where Wells Fargo was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 4.00%. Representative corridors: US to Mexico 4.12%. Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin Wells Fargo applied above the interbank rate, across its 23 priced services in 9 corridors, was 0.86%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). Wells Fargo's page says fees and exchange rates are shown upfront. Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: On December 20, 2022 the CFPB ordered Wells Fargo to pay more than $2 billion in consumer redress and a $1.7 billion penalty for violations across auto loans, mortgages and deposit accounts, including wrongful repossessions, frozen accounts and improper overdraft fees. Scored 80, minus 55 for one of the largest consumer-protection orders the CFPB has issued.

accessibility.note: Wells Fargo's ExpressSend page says it supports transfers to Mexico, the Caribbean, Central America, South America and Asia, sent from the Wells Fargo Mobile app; customers who accept the mobile terms can no longer use it at a branch or by phone. Only Wells Fargo customers can send.

links.label: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: Stablecoin route (USDC via an exchange)
products.description: Buying a dollar stablecoin such as USDC, sending it on a blockchain and having the recipient sell it on an exchange in their country. Can be fast and cheap on the sending side, but the cash-out cost varies by country and exchange, and a mistaken or scam payment usually cannot be reversed.

complaints.note: The FTC's consumer guidance says 'Cryptocurrency payments typically are not reversible.' and that cryptocurrency held in accounts is not insured by a government the way an FDIC-insured bank deposit is. A stablecoin transfer is not a regulated remittance with a cancellation window or an error-resolution process behind it. Scored 20 for recourse rather than for any one company's record.

accessibility.note: Circle's USDC page says USDC is available in 185+ countries and is redeemable 1:1 for US dollars, but that 'Circle Mint enables exchanges, institutional traders, banks, and large financial institutions to directly redeem USDC 1:1 for USD from Circle.' A household sender and recipient therefore each need an exchange account and a working local cash-out route.

links.label: FTC: what to know about cryptocurrency and scams

products.name: Paysend
products.description: A UK-based digital transfer service sending to cards, accounts, wallets and cash pickup in 170+ countries, strong on routes to Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Low cost in the World Bank sample.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 25 corridors where Paysend was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 1.82%. Representative corridors: UK to India 1.20%. Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin Paysend applied above the interbank rate, across its 57 priced services in 25 corridors, was 1.21%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). Paysend's UK site says its rate and fee are always shown before you confirm. Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: No consumer-protection enforcement action against Paysend appears in the CFPB's list of remittance enforcement actions (checked October 2026). The CFPB complaint database holds 14 complaints filed under Paysend US LLC about money transfer services received January 2024 to December 2025, a raw count not adjusted for customer numbers. Paysend Plc is authorised by the FCA as an electronic money institution (FRN 900004), per its own site. Scored 80, the method's starting point for a clean record.

accessibility.note: Paysend's UK site says it sends to 170+ countries from the phone, to an account, card, e-wallet or cash.

links.label: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: TransferGo
products.description: A European digital transfer service popular for sending between the UK, EU and Eastern Europe. The cheapest provider in this comparison in the World Bank's sample of its corridors.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 12 corridors where TransferGo was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 0.47%. TransferGo was priced mostly on intra-European routes (UK to Poland 0.40%, Poland to Ukraine 0.10%). Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin TransferGo applied above the interbank rate, across its 38 priced services in 12 corridors, was 0.78%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). TransferGo's own fee page lists currency exchange on transfers from 0.5%. Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

accessibility.note: TransferGo's fees page says transfers go to over 160 countries, to bank accounts or cards, from the app or web, with a free multi-currency account.

links.label: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide dataset

products.name: Taptap Send
products.description: An app for sending money to Africa, Asia and Latin America, often with no fee and a rate at or above interbank in the World Bank sample. Coverage is a list of a few dozen countries rather than the whole world.

fees.note: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Q3 2025 survey (complete dataset, catalogue updated September 2026): across the 5 corridors where Taptap Send was priced from the US, UK or an EU country, the median of its cheapest service's total cost for sending the equivalent of $200 (transfer fee plus exchange-rate margin) was 1.23%. Taptap Send was priced in five corridors only (for example UK to Ghana 0.97%). Score = 100 minus 10 points per percentage point of cost.

transparency.note: In the same World Bank Q3 2025 data, the median exchange-rate margin Taptap Send applied above the interbank rate, across its 5 priced services in 5 corridors, was -0.20%: the part of the cost carried inside the rate rather than shown as a fee. The World Bank recorded every one of these services as transparent (the rate was disclosed to the researcher). A negative margin means the rate was better than interbank at the time, which is a subsidy rather than a hidden charge; the sample is small. Score = 100 minus 15 points per percentage point of margin.

complaints.note: No consumer-protection enforcement action against Taptap Send appears in the CFPB's list of remittance enforcement actions (checked October 2026). The CFPB complaint database holds 54 complaints filed under TapTap Send Inc. about money transfer services received January 2024 to December 2025, a raw count not adjusted for customer numbers. Scored 80, the method's starting point for a clean record.

accessibility.note: Taptap Send's site lists the countries it currently serves (around seventy, across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Europe) and offers bank deposits, mobile money and cash pickups. Sending is app-only.
